Danmark represents the national level of analysis in the 2024 evaluation of adult ADHD care, serving as the overarching reference frame for regional variation across the country's psychiatric departments [^src1]. In the context of the first public reporting of [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]]—a new quality indicator measuring the assessment of social support needs within 120 days of treatment initiation—Denmark's national performance highlights significant systemic documentation challenges [^src1].

At the national level, only 37% (95% CI: 35–38) of adult ADHD patients had their social support needs assessed within the required timeframe [^src1]. This figure falls substantially short of the 90% development target [^src1]. The low fulfillment rates observed across Denmark are attributed primarily to inadequate registration practices rather than a lack of actual clinical assessment, prompting recommendations for improved administrative routines rather than changes to the indicator itself [^src1].
